body:
> Label-based indexing without slicing should be possible with .loc even when the dataframe is not lexsorted

Notice this is specific to indexing with lists (and booleans, but not single labels). Anyway, I'll push a PR in minutes.

Great!

To add one perhaps self-evident corner case: in a multi-indexed df, ':'
should be permissible as well.

df.loc[['a', 'c'], :, ['two', 'one']]

This is not a tested code example. But the idea should be clear: If the
slice captures the entire row/col, sorting should not be required either.

issue.title: BUG: do not raise UnsortedIndexError if sorting is not required

repository.name: pandas
repository.description: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more
